title: Augmentation spectral sequence for a total simplicial site
statement:
Let $\mathcal C$ be a small site with finite limits [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology, def-weil-size-convention], let $X\in\mathcal C$, and let $U_\bullet\to X$ be an augmented simplicial object [def-weil-pbc-simplicial-object]. Give the slice sites and the total site the induced topologies, write $\mathcal T=\mathrm{Sh}((\mathcal C/U_\bullet)_{total})$, and let $b: \mathcal T\to\mathrm{Sh}(\mathcal C/X)$ and $b_p:\mathrm{Sh}(\mathcal C/U_p)\to\mathrm{Sh}(\mathcal C/X)$ be the augmentation and component localization geometric morphisms [def-trf-geometric-morphism]. An abelian sheaf $F$ on $\mathcal T$ is a family of abelian sheaves $F_p$ on $\mathcal C/U_p$ with transition maps $u_\alpha^{-1}F_p\to F_q$ for the structure maps $u_\alpha:U_q\to U_p$, satisfying identity and composition. Write $R^qb_{p,*}$ for the right derived functors of $b_{p,*}$ and $Rb_*$ for the derived direct image [def-sp-left-exact-additive]. Let $C_b(F)$ be the nonnegative cochain complex with $C_b(F)^p=b_{p,*}F_p$ and differential the alternating sum of the face maps, the $i$-th face map being induced by $F_p\to u_{i,*}u_i^{-1}F_p\to u_{i,*}F_{p+1}$ and $b_{p+1}=b_pu_i$. Let $e:b_*F\to b_{0,*}F_0$ be the map adjoint, under $b_0^{-1}\dashv b_{0,*}$, to the degree-zero component $b_0^{-1}b_*F\to F_0$ of the counit $b^{-1}b_*F\to F$; it lands in $\ker(C_b(F)^0\to C_b(F)^1)=H^0(C_b(F))$. For every such $F$, regarded in degree zero, there is a natural first-quadrant spectral sequence
$$E_1^{p,q}=R^q b_{p,*}F_p\Longrightarrow H^{p+q}(Rb_*F),\qquad p,q\ge0,$$
whose $d_1$ is the alternating sum of the face maps induced by the transition maps of $F$. The double-complex construction also supplies a canonical natural comparison $\kappa_F:C_b(F)\to Rb_*F$ [def-weil-abstract-derived-category], and the $q=0$ edge of the spectral sequence is the map on cohomology induced by $\kappa_F$. In degree zero, $H^0(\kappa_F)\circ e:b_*F\to H^0(Rb_*F)$ is the canonical identification $b_*F=R^0b_*F=H^0(Rb_*F)$.

source.place: Tag 0D7A, lemma-augmentation-spectral-sequence, including the double-complex proof and its canonical comparison; the alternating-face identification is the displayed E_1 differential.

proof.text: The slice-site construction supplies the augmentation $b$ and its component inverse images $(b^{-1}G)_p=b_p^{-1}G$. Its transition adjunctions make $p\mapsto b_{p,*}F_p$ cosimplicial. The identities for two successive cofaces pair terms with opposite signs, so the alternating differential squares to zero. The degree-zero counit component defining $e$ is compatible with the two vertices of $[1]$, hence its two coface images agree and $\delta^0e=0$. More explicitly, a map $G\to b_*F$ is a compatible family $b_p^{-1}G\to F_p$; its degree-zero map extends along each vertex $[0]\to[p]$. Equality along the two vertices of $[1]$ makes the extensions along any two vertices agree, by the map $[1]\to[p]$ joining them. These extensions satisfy all simplicial operators. Thus $e$ in fact identifies $b_*F$ with $H^0(C_b(F))$, with exactly the stated counit normalization.

source.place: Tag 0D79, lemma-augmentation-cech-complex, degree-zero equalizer and adjunction; Tag 09WL for the slice-site augmentation

proof.text: The slice sites and the total site are small. Their abelian sheaves have enough injectives; they are also the modules over the constant integer sheaf, hence Grothendieck abelian. Choose a nonnegative injective representative $QI^\bullet\cong F[0]$ by the bounded-below representative theorem with lower bound zero. It is K-injective. The bijection of homotopy-category maps into a K-injective with derived-category maps represents the inverse isomorphism by a chain map $F[0]\to I^\bullet$; it is a quasi-isomorphism, hence an injective resolution under $F$. The derived-injective computation identifies $b_*I^\bullet$ with $Rb_*F$. Exact component restriction sends each $I^q$ to an injective sheaf $I_p^q$ and sends the resolution to an injective resolution of $F_p$. Consequently $H^q(b_{p,*}I_p^\bullet)=R^qb_{p,*}F_p$, including $H^0=b_{p,*}F_p$, by the definition of the right derived functors.

Form $A^{p,q}=b_{p,*}I_p^q$ for $p,q\ge0$, zero otherwise. Its horizontal differential is the alternating face differential and its vertical differential is induced by $I^\bullet$. Naturality of transitions makes these differentials commute. Totalize with $d_h+(-1)^pd_v$. For every fixed $q$, the injective augmentation exactness lemma applies to $I^q$: the augmented horizontal row $0\to b_*I^q\to A^{0,q}\to A^{1,q}\to\cdots$ is exact. Naturality of its augmentation in $I^q$ makes the inclusions $b_*I^q\to A^{0,q}$ a chain map $\rho:b_*I^\bullet\to\operatorname{Tot}A$; its horizontal differential is zero and the vertical sign at $p=0$ is $+1$.

Apply the first-quadrant resolution-column augmentation lemma with $K=A$, with the first index the face degree, and with the nonnegative complex $b_*I^\bullet$. Its chain map into $K.X\,0$ is given by the row augmentations of Step 3, and its composite with $K.d\,0\,1$ is zero. For each internal degree $q$, its resolution column $K.\mathrm{flip}.X\,q$ is the horizontal row $A^{\bullet,q}$. Step 3 says that $b_*I^q[0]\to A^{\bullet,q}$ is a quasi-isomorphism. The lemma therefore makes the explicitly constructed $\rho$ a quasi-isomorphism. Thus in the derived category $\operatorname{Tot}A$ is identified with $b_*I^\bullet$, and hence with $Rb_*F$ by Step 2. The first-quadrant bounds give finitely many summands in every total degree, as required.

The first double-complex spectral sequence, applied to $A$, has $E_1^{p,q}=H^q(A^{p,\bullet})$ and $d_1$ induced by the horizontal differential. Step 2 identifies these terms with $R^qb_{p,*}F_p$ and their differentials with the alternating sums induced by the transition maps of $F$: the maps on the resolution columns are precisely the adjoint coface maps used to define $C_b$. Both indices are nonnegative, so the cited theorem gives convergence with finite filtration on each $H^n(\operatorname{Tot}A)$. Transporting the abutment through $\rho$ gives $H^n(Rb_*F)$. This yields the asserted first-quadrant spectral sequence without imposing any hypercover hypothesis.

The resolution map gives a chain map $j:C_b(F)\to\operatorname{Tot}A$: in degree $p$ use $b_{p,*}F_p\to b_{p,*}I_p^0=A^{p,0}$ and the $(p,0)$ diagonal inclusion. Its vertical differential is zero, and naturality gives the horizontal chain-map identity. Set $\kappa_F=\rho^{-1}j$ in the derived category, using the derived identification of Step 4. Left exactness of $b_{p,*}$ identifies $b_{p,*}F_p$ with the vertical cycles in $A^{p,0}$ (there are no vertical boundaries from degree $-1$). Thus $E_2^{p,0}=H^p(C_b(F))$. A class on this row represented by a horizontal cocycle is sent by $j$ to that same cocycle in the total complex. In the column filtration this is exactly the bottom edge: it passes to the surviving quotient $E_\infty^{p,0}$ and then to $F^pH^p(\operatorname{Tot}A)\subset H^p(\operatorname{Tot}A)$. This proves the asserted edge normalization after composing with $\rho^{-1}$.

A morphism $F\to F^{\prime}$ gives a derived morphism $QI\to QI^{\prime}$ through the resolution identifications. The bijection of homotopy-category maps into the K-injective $I^{\prime}$ with derived-category maps supplies a chain-map lift uniquely up to homotopy. The K-injective comparison lemma identifies these with the canonical resolution comparisons. Applying component restriction and $b_{p,*}$ gives a map of the double complexes commuting with $j$ and $\rho$. A homotopy of these lifts induces the total homotopy with sign $(-1)^p$ on the summand of face degree $p$; the horizontal cross terms cancel. It preserves the column filtration and gives vertically homotopic maps on every column, hence identical maps on $E_1$ and on all subsequent pages. The same total homotopy proves equality of the maps in the derived category. Comparison lifts for identity maps between two choices of resolution are inverse up to homotopy; their composites compare to the identity. Consequently both the spectral sequence from $E_1$ onward and $\kappa_F$ are independent of the resolution, with canonical comparisons compatible with composition. They are natural in $F$.

Write $i:F\to I^0$ for the resolution augmentation. Naturality of the counit defining $e$ gives, in total degree zero, $j^0e=e_{I^0}\,b_*i=\rho^0\,b_*i$. All three maps land in cycles, so on degree-zero cohomology $H^0(j)\,e=H^0(\rho)\,H^0(b_*i)$. Left exactness identifies the kernel of $b_*I^0\to b_*I^1$ with $b_*F$ through $b_*i$. By the definition of $R^0b_*$ this is the canonical identification $b_*F=R^0b_*F=H^0(Rb_*F)$. Composing the displayed equality with $H^0(\rho)^{-1}$ proves $H^0(\kappa_F)\circ e$ is precisely that identification, as claimed.

tool_uses.why: Small-site module categories with the constant integer ring give Grothendieck abelian categories; no trace-unit lemma supplies this generic fact.
The generic first-quadrant augmentation-to-total criterion identifies the injective-row total with the pushforward resolution; this is homological algebra, not a replacement of the unit route.
The two first-quadrant spectral sequences supply the E1 page and finite convergence of the constructed bicomplex.
Generic uniqueness up to homotopy of injective resolution comparisons supplies naturality and independence of choices.
The homotopy-to-derived Hom bijection into a K-injective realizes the resolution augmentation and lifts coefficient morphisms; it is a general homological tool.
